title: Constructible exceptional composition and its counit characterization
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [sk-def-sf-setting]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$. Let $X,Y,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-morphisms; put $x=g\circ f$. Use the constructible finite-Tor categories $\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}=\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ and the specified operations of [sk-def-sf-operations], with derived-complete integral, raw rationalized and common-finite-stage coefficients. Write $F_{h,\Lambda}=Rh_{!,\Lambda}$, $G_{h,\Lambda}=Rh^!_\Lambda$ and $\epsilon_{h,\Lambda}$ for the counits of their constructible adjunctions $F_{h,\Lambda}\dashv G_{h,\Lambda}$ at every stage [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients], for $h=f,g,x$. For a finite extension $E\subset E'$ the same notation at the target coefficient stages uses $E'$ in place of $E$, as in that node.

Write $\alpha_\Lambda:F_{g,\Lambda}F_{f,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{x,\Lambda}$ for the canonical compactification compositor: at finite level the composition isomorphism of [thm-sf-comp-composition], restricted to the finite-Tor constructible categories, and at the integral, rational and common stages its completed integral form and its rationalized/common-stage forms. Let $c_\Lambda:G_{f,\Lambda}G_{g,\Lambda}\to G_{x,\Lambda}$ denote the conjugate of $\alpha_\Lambda^{-1}$ under the composite adjunction and $F_{x,\Lambda}\dashv G_{x,\Lambda}$, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate].

For every $\Lambda\in\{A_n,R,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ this gives a canonical natural isomorphism $c_\Lambda$ of the actual constructible functors. For $K\in\mathcal C_{X,\Lambda}$ and $L\in\mathcal C_{Z,\Lambda}$ its action on Hom groups is the composite
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,G_fG_gL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(F_gF_fK,L)\xrightarrow{h\mapsto h\circ\alpha_K^{-1}}\operatorname{Hom}_Z(F_xK,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,G_xL).$$
Suppressing $\Lambda$, the component $c_L$ is uniquely characterized by
$$\epsilon_{x,L}\circ F_x(c_L)\circ\alpha_{G_fG_gL}=\epsilon_{g,L}\circ F_g(\epsilon_{f,G_gL}).$$
The comparison is independent of compactification choices under the specified refinement identifications. It is natural in $L$ and respects the canonical integer-shift identifications of these exact adjunctions. These assertions use only the constructible exceptional adjoints, with no unrestricted ambient exceptional-adjoint datum.

proof.text: The data module establishes normalized integral realization equality by projection extensionality and the Milnor finite-group argument. Apply [lem-sf-constructible-left-compositor-coherence] for the geometric canonical left compositors, coefficient normalizations, shift compatibility and left refinement squares.

Conjugate inverse alpha through the composite adjunction and the direct adjunction. The Mathlib conjugate counit equation proves the pasted counit. Its Hom bijection and cancellation prove the Hom action and componentwise uniqueness.

The counit condition identifies each right refinement with the conjugate of its left comparison. Apply conjugateEquiv composition and whiskering to the left refinement square to obtain the displayed right refinement equation.
Install the adjunction shift instances from their unitShift and counitShift fields. The existing source-library conjugate shift instance yields the exceptional mate shift from left-alpha shift.
